example_prompt.user:
Write 12 short stories that a 3-year-old can understand, using only very simple words.

Rules for every story:
- 150 to 200 words each. Simple sentences. Only words a 3-year-old knows.
- Every story is about printers, printing or paper (see its topic below). The printer or the paper matters in the story from the beginning to the end; it is not just mentioned once.
- In every story someone prints something, or printing goes wrong, and that is what the story is about.
- Each story must make sense: a clear beginning, middle and end, and things happen for a reason, the way they could in a child's day. Use the required words in a natural way; if a word does not fit well, use it in a small side moment.
- A printer can be a normal machine or, sometimes, a friendly machine that can talk or feel, but it stays on its table and does printer things: it hums, beeps, takes paper and prints. It does not walk, eat or drive.
- Write like a children's picture book: plain, warm and concrete. No big words, no grown-up things (no money, jobs, bosses or meetings), no technical words.
- Do not start the stories the same way. Use "Once upon a time" in at most two of them. Each story has its own characters.
- Plain text only: no title, no headings, no bold, no lists, no emoji. Straight quotes only.

Story 1: about a printer that moves to a new room. Use the noun "friend", the verb "count" and the adjective "clean". A rabbit is in the story (it can be printed in a picture); the word "rabbit" must appear in the first three sentences. One character is named Lucy. The story should have the following features: the story has some sort of conflict.
Story 2: about an office at night, after everyone has gone home. Use the noun "flower", the verb "drink" and the adjective "careful". An apple is in the story (it can be printed in a picture); the word "apple" must appear in the first three sentences. The story should have the following features: the story has a sad ending (gentle, nothing scary).
Story 3: about a puppy that runs off with a printed page. Use the noun "letter", the verb "help" and the adjective "sticky". A tree is in the story (it can be printed in a picture); the word "tree" must appear in the first three sentences. The story should have the following features: something unexpected happens, the story has a sad ending (gentle, nothing scary).
Story 4: about an old printer that is very slow. Use the noun "wind", the verb "tape" and the adjective "dull". A dog is in the story (it can be printed in a picture); the word "dog" must appear in the first three sentences. The story should have the following features: something unexpected happens.
Story 5: about a printer's blinking light. Use the noun "garden", the verb "tape" and the adjective "messy". An apple is in the story (it can be printed in a picture); the word "apple" must appear in the first three sentences. The story should have the following features: the story should contain at least one dialogue, the story teaches a simple lesson.
Story 6: about a blank sheet of paper that wants to become a picture. Use the noun "soup", the verb "kick" and the adjective "cool". One character is named Will. The story should have the following features: the story has a small hint early on of what will happen later, something unexpected happens.
Story 7: about a child who is allowed to press the print button. Use the noun "bunny", the verb "shut" and the adjective "funny". One character is named Sara. The story should have the following features: the story has a sad ending (gentle, nothing scary).
Story 8: about a tall stack of paper that falls over. Use the noun "train", the verb "chase" and the adjective "sour". The story should have the following features: something unexpected happens, the story has a happy ending.
Story 9: about a printer and a scanner who are best friends. Use the noun "rug", the verb "climb" and the adjective "careful". A frog is in the story (it can be printed in a picture); the word "frog" must appear in the first three sentences. The story should have the following features: the story teaches a simple lesson.
Story 10: about a child printing a birthday card. Use the noun "cat", the verb "tape" and the adjective "light". One character is named Sue. The story should have the following features: the story has a small hint early on of what will happen later, the story should contain at least one dialogue.
Story 11: about a new printer coming to a family's home. Use the noun "coat", the verb "stand" and the adjective "dry". A sun is in the story (it can be printed in a picture); the word "sun" must appear in the first three sentences. The story should have the following features: the story should contain at least one dialogue.
Story 12: about a printer that prints invitations for a party. Use the noun "pillow", the verb "play" and the adjective "angry". A flower is in the story (it can be printed in a picture); the word "flower" must appear in the first three sentences. The story should have the following features: the story has a happy ending, the story has some sort of conflict.

Output format, exactly:
### STORY 1
<story 1 text>
### STORY 2
<story 2 text>
...
### STORY 12
<story 12 text>
### END
Write nothing before the first ### line and nothing after ### END. Remember to only use simple words!
